name: Dynasort
summary: Shopify app that re-sorts collections, variant lists, search results and upsell blocks automatically, using recipes built from 60+ signals such as sales, margin, inventory and reviews.
best_for: Shopify stores with large or fast-changing catalogues where product order is a merchandising decision (seasonal ranges, frequent stock-outs, wide margin spreads) and nobody who wants to re-order collections by hand every week.
skip_if: your catalogue is small enough for one person to curate in an afternoon, the order barely changes, or you are not on Shopify: at $99 a month for the first paid tier, the sorting has to be earning its fee
honest_knock: Sorting driven by 40+ blended signals is powerful and opaque in the same breath: a recipe that ranks by margin, velocity and stock at once will sometimes bury a product you wanted seen, and there is real trial and error in getting the recipes to match how you actually merchandise. The jump from free to paid is steep at $99 a month, and it buys capacity rather than capability: search, recommendations and post-purchase are already in the free Demo, and Basic multiplies collections, recipes and serves (100,000 a month against 10,000). Above that the cards were printed under each other's headings in September and early October 2026; they read correctly on 17 November 2026, and A/B testing and the connector API sit on the free Demo card. And the evidence base is thin: 14 reviews, with thirteen fives and a single one-star and nothing in between. It is Shopify-only, so it is not an option if any part of your catalogue lives elsewhere.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/dynasort and in our own test the same day; earlier reads 14 and 15 September and 3 October 2026) Four tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days. Demo is free for as long as you like: 2 sorted and 2 managed collections, 10 recipes built from 40+ signals, a sort refresh every 60 minutes, variant sorting on 2 products, 10,000 recommendation serves a month, A/B testing and collection analytics, and a connector API for your stack or an LLM. Basic is $99 a month and adds, on top of Demo, 25 sorted and 10 managed collections, 20 recipes, a refresh every 30 minutes, variant sorting on 50 products, 100,000 serves a month and Customers Also Bought recipes. Pro is $249 a month for 100 sorted and 25 managed collections, 50 recipes, a refresh every 20 minutes, variant sorting on 200 products, 1 million serves a month, mobile versus desktop analytics, 30 day serving analytics and A/B tests of recommendation recipes. Enterprise is $499 a month for 1,000 sorted and 100 managed collections, 250 recipes, a refresh every 10 minutes, variant sorting on 5,000 products, unlimited serves, 365 day analytics with custom ranges and priority support and onboarding. Every paid tier carries a 30 day free trial. The mix up we recorded on 14 September and again on 3 October 2026, with the Pro and Enterprise capacity blocks under each other's headings, is gone: on 17 November 2026 the Pro card listed the 100 collection allowance and the Enterprise card the 1,000 collection allowance. The prices have not moved. In our own test on a Shopify development store the app showed a banner, “Special pricing for your store”, with Basic, Pro and Enterprise marked down by half ($99 to $49, $249 to $124 and $499 to $249) and an end date six days away; that is a temporary offer on the app's screen and not on the listing, so we do not count it as the price. The app's own text said any plan is free for 30 days, “You pay $0 today”, with a first charge on 17 December 2026. We chose Demo and saw no payment screen. The listing's rating block read 4.6 from 14 reviews, thirteen five star and one one star.

measured.tested_by: Our team; actor, account and scope are documented in the review.
method: Installed on a Shopify development store and timed the first synchronisation
Applied the default sort rule to one collection and checked the result in the Shopify admin
Read the plan page and the uninstall dialog without paying

claims.claim: Setting up your store: about 5 minutes remaining
claims.observed: The app said about 5 minutes remaining while syncing 3 collections, 23 products and 2 recent orders; it took more than 7 minutes before the store was ready, and the first sorted result stood on screen about 8 minutes after the install.
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The wording of the setup screen against one run on a store of 23 products; larger stores and other days were not tried, so the duration is not set against a fixed claim.
claims.buying_consequence: Expect to wait longer than the app says before the first sort; the wait was a synchronisation of a very small store.

claims.claim: Processing is not turned on yet. Go to Settings to enable it.
claims.observed: After the Dynasort Status was set to Active and saved, the app said that processing was not turned on; Processing had to be switched On in Settings (interval 60 minutes) before the collection was sorted.
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The message of the app against the result after the switch; no other setting or plan was compared.
claims.buying_consequence: Setting a collection to Active is not enough: the collection stays unsorted until Processing is switched On in Settings, one extra step the app only shows afterwards.

claims.claim: Sales (Last 30 Days) (100), Sales (All Time) (50), Inventory Quantity (50), Sold Out (-100), On Sale (-20), Variants In Stock (100)
claims.observed: After Sync now the page showed Sorting 1 minute ago, and the sort choice in Shopify changed from Most relevant to Manually with the products in the order and scores of the app (150, 150, 127, 127).
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The recipe and scores of the app against the product order in the Shopify admin on one smart collection; the online store itself was not checked.
claims.buying_consequence: One switch sorted a collection of 8 products by itself, with no dragging; the Shopify sort choice changes to Manually while the app is active.

claims.observed: The collection of 8 products held no sold out product, so the setting Sold out items: Move to bottom was not seen at work.
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The Sold out setting of the recipe against a collection without any sold out product; nothing could be compared.
claims.buying_consequence: Whether sold out products really drop to the bottom is not shown by this test; check it on a collection that contains a sold out product.

claims.observed: After the Dynasort Status was set to Off and saved, the Shopify sort choice stayed on Manually instead of returning to Most relevant; it was set back by hand and the original order returned.
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The recipe setting Revert To (When Off) against the Shopify sort choice some minutes after Status Off; a longer wait or a later processing run was not tried.
claims.buying_consequence: Switching Dynasort off does not by itself put the collection back; a merchant has to reset the sort choice in Shopify.

claims.claim: Try any plan free for 30 days. You pay $0 today.
claims.observed: The paid plans were not clicked, so the free trial and the Shopify approval screen were not seen; the free Demo plan was chosen instead and opened with no card or billing screen.
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The trial text of the plan page against a Shopify approval screen that never appeared; no paid plan was started.
claims.buying_consequence: The trial wording is on the plan page, but whether a paid plan really costs $0 today was not tested; the free Demo plan was.

claims.observed: A banner in the app showed Basic $49, Pro $124 and Enterprise $249 a month, half of the crossed out $99, $249 and $499, which are the App Store prices; the banner said the offer ends in 6 days. Only reported, not compared with a price field.
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The discounted prices in the app against the crossed out list prices on the same plan page; the discount is temporary and tied to the store, so no stored price was compared.
claims.buying_consequence: The app showed half of the App Store prices for this store for a limited time; the price you see can differ from the listing and can end after a few days.

claims.observed: The plan page lists 2, 25, 100 and 1000 sorted collections for Demo, Basic, Pro and Enterprise, with processing schedules of 60, 30, 20 and 10 minutes. The App Store listing now shows the collection counts in the right column, while the dossier still describes the mislabelled plan cards of October.
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The plan page of the app against the current App Store listing; the October state of the listing was not seen in this test.
claims.buying_consequence: The plan page and the listing agree on the collection counts; the dossier text about mislabelled cards no longer matches the listing.

claims.observed: The plan page shows Basic at $99 a month crossed out and $49 a month, Pro $249 crossed out and $124, Enterprise $499 crossed out and $249. The paid plans were not clicked, so no approval screen, total, tax or renewal term was seen.
claims.plan: Free Demo plan only; the paid plans were not clicked
claims.comparability: The prices on the plan cards against a Shopify approval screen that never appeared; no tax, term or stored cost rule was compared.
claims.buying_consequence: The price you would pay for a paid plan is not confirmed by a Shopify approval screen; start with the free Demo plan and check the screen before you approve a paid plan.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Dynasort (collection sorting) on a Shopify development store: the install, the free Demo plan without a card or billing screen, the first synchronisation (more than 7 minutes, where the app said about 5), the sort rule on Automated Collection (8 products) with the recipe Dynasort Default, the message that Processing had to be switched On in Settings first, the result in Shopify (the sort choice changed from Most relevant to Manually in the order of the app scores, about 8 minutes and 14 steps after the install), the switch back (Shopify stayed on Manually until the sort choice was reset by hand), the plan page with a temporary 50% discount (Basic $49, Pro $124, Enterprise $249 a month) and the uninstall, which asks for a reason. Nothing was paid or approved. Install: the app (App Store name Dynasort Collection Sorting, developer Dyna, Denver; Built for Shopify; rating 4.6 from 14 reviews) was installed from its App Store listing through the install form in our own tab. The install started at 22:12 (clock of the test computer). The permission screen said that the app needs access to view customer data, view staff and contributor data and view and edit store data; it was approved with Install. The app opened as Dynasort from Dyna, the same product as the listing, on its Plans page. Plan choice: the free Demo plan was chosen with the button Go Demo. No card and no billing screen came up. A welcome screen asked for a goal; Better merchandised collections was chosen and Build my setup plan was clicked. Wait: the screen Setting up your store said about 5 minutes remaining and Syncing 3 collections, 23 products, and 2 recent orders. It took more than 7 minutes before it said Your store is ready. Core action: the app listed the collections Hydrogen (3 products), Automated Collection (8 products) and Home page (0), with the recipe Dynasort Default, status Off and the text 0/2 Sorted. Automated Collection, a smart collection, was chosen. In Shopify it was sorted Most relevant before the test. The recipe Dynasort Default weighs Sales (Last 30 Days) (100), Sales (All Time) (50), Inventory Quantity (50), Sold Out (-100), On Sale (-20) and Variants In Stock (100), with the tie breaker Best selling and Sold out items set to Move to bottom, and Revert To (When Off) set to Most relevant. The Dynasort Status was set to Active and saved (Collection saved). The status box is a native select inside an iframe, so a mouse click could not open it; pressing Escape and then typing the first letter (A for Active, O for Off) worked. A message then said that processing is not turned on yet and that Dynasort will not auto-sort the collections otherwise. In Settings, Processing was switched from Off to On (interval 60 minutes) and saved. After Sync now and about 1 to 2 minutes, the page showed Sorting 1 minute ago (about 22:20). The first result therefore came about 8 minutes after the install, most of it waiting for the first synchronisation, in about 14 steps. Result in Shopify: the sort choice of the collection changed from Most relevant to Manually, and the order became The Multi-location Snowboard, The Multi-managed Snowboard, The Complete Snowboard, The Collection Snowboard: Liquid, then the products Hidden, Hydrogen and Compare at Price, equal to the order and scores in the app (150, 150, 127, 127 and so on). The collection holds no sold out product, so the rule Sold Out (-100) with Move to bottom was not seen at work. Switching back: the Dynasort Status was set to Off and saved, but Shopify stayed on Manually; the revert to Most relevant did not happen at once. The sort choice was set back to Most relevant by hand in Shopify and saved, and the original order returned. A merchant who switches the app off should check the sort choice of the collection. Plans: a banner says Special pricing for your store and that Basic, Pro and Enterprise are discounted for the store, starting at $49/mo, and that the offer ends in 6 days. Plan page: Demo Free; Basic $99/mo crossed out, $49/mo; Pro $249/mo crossed out, $124/mo; Enterprise $499/mo crossed out, $249/mo, so 50% off the list price in the app. The text says: Try any plan free for 30 days. You pay $0 today. Your first charge would be on December 17, 2026, and you can cancel anytime before then from your Shopify admin. The discount is temporary and tied to the store; the App Store listing shows $99, $249 and $499 without a discount. Sorted collections per plan: Demo 2, Basic 25, Pro 100, Enterprise 1000; processing schedule Demo 60 min, Basic 30, Pro 20, Enterprise 10. Demo has no Customers Also Bought recipes and no device analytics. The App Store listing now shows the collection counts in the right column; the dossier still describes the mislabelled plan cards seen in October. Checkout: the free Demo plan was chosen, the paid plans were not clicked, so no Shopify approval screen, no total, no test charge and no card field was seen. Nothing was approved. Cancelling: no paid plan was started. In Settings, Apps, Uninstall opened the dialog Uninstall Dynasort?, which says that the app can no longer be used, that data managed by the app will be deleted and that a request will be sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason for uninstalling is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled at about 22:22 after the evidence was complete and is gone from the installed apps. Not tested: the paid plans and the free trial, the A/B test, a sold out product moving to the bottom, variant sorting, recommendations, the effect in the online store (only the Shopify admin was checked), a large catalogue, Insights (data appears after 24 hours) and Sort rotation. Clean up: the collection order was set back to Most relevant, the Dynasort Status was set to Off, Processing had been switched On in the app and disappeared with the uninstall, the app was uninstalled and our own tab was closed. No other app was touched. The price fields are not changed here. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app did not sort until Processing was switched On in Settings, which the app only said after the status was set to Active. The first synchronisation took more than 7 minutes (the app said about 5). The sort choice of the collection in Shopify changes to Manually, and after the app was switched off Shopify stayed on Manually until the sort choice was reset by hand. The paid plans showed a temporary discount in the app that the App Store listing does not show, and the dossier still describes the mislabelled plan cards of October.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Dynasort (collection sorting) on a Shopify development store: the install, the free Demo plan without a card or billing screen, the first synchronisation (more than 7 minutes, where the app said about 5), the sort rule on Automated Collection (8 products) with the recipe Dynasort Default, the message that Processing had to be switched On in Settings first, the result in Shopify (the sort choice changed from Most relevant to Manually in the order of the app scores, about 8 minutes and 14 steps after the install), the switch back (Shopify stayed on Manually until the sort choice was reset by hand), the plan page with a temporary 50% discount (Basic $49, Pro $124, Enterprise $249 a month) and the uninstall, which asks for a reason. Nothing was paid or approved. Install: the app (App Store name Dynasort Collection Sorting, developer Dyna, Denver; Built for Shopify; rating 4.6 from 14 reviews) was installed from its App Store listing through the install form in our own tab. The install started at 22:12 (clock of the test computer). The permission screen said that the app needs access to view customer data, view staff and contributor data and view and edit store data; it was approved with Install. The app opened as Dynasort from Dyna, the same product as the listing, on its Plans page. Plan choice: the free Demo plan was chosen with the button Go Demo. No card and no billing screen came up. A welcome screen asked for a goal; Better merchandised collections was chosen and Build my setup plan was clicked. Wait: the screen Setting up your store said about 5 minutes remaining and Syncing 3 collections, 23 products, and 2 recent orders. It took more than 7 minutes before it said Your store is ready. Core action: the app listed the collections Hydrogen (3 products), Automated Collection (8 products) and Home page (0), with the recipe Dynasort Default, status Off and the text 0/2 Sorted. Automated Collection, a smart collection, was chosen. In Shopify it was sorted Most relevant before the test. The recipe Dynasort Default weighs Sales (Last 30 Days) (100), Sales (All Time) (50), Inventory Quantity (50), Sold Out (-100), On Sale (-20) and Variants In Stock (100), with the tie breaker Best selling and Sold out items set to Move to bottom, and Revert To (When Off) set to Most relevant. The Dynasort Status was set to Active and saved (Collection saved). The status box is a native select inside an iframe, so a mouse click could not open it; pressing Escape and then typing the first letter (A for Active, O for Off) worked. A message then said that processing is not turned on yet and that Dynasort will not auto-sort the collections otherwise. In Settings, Processing was switched from Off to On (interval 60 minutes) and saved. After Sync now and about 1 to 2 minutes, the page showed Sorting 1 minute ago (about 22:20). The first result therefore came about 8 minutes after the install, most of it waiting for the first synchronisation, in about 14 steps. Result in Shopify: the sort choice of the collection changed from Most relevant to Manually, and the order became The Multi-location Snowboard, The Multi-managed Snowboard, The Complete Snowboard, The Collection Snowboard: Liquid, then the products Hidden, Hydrogen and Compare at Price, equal to the order and scores in the app (150, 150, 127, 127 and so on). The collection holds no sold out product, so the rule Sold Out (-100) with Move to bottom was not seen at work. Switching back: the Dynasort Status was set to Off and saved, but Shopify stayed on Manually; the revert to Most relevant did not happen at once. The sort choice was set back to Most relevant by hand in Shopify and saved, and the original order returned. A merchant who switches the app off should check the sort choice of the collection. Plans: a banner says Special pricing for your store and that Basic, Pro and Enterprise are discounted for the store, starting at $49/mo, and that the offer ends in 6 days. Plan page: Demo Free; Basic $99/mo crossed out, $49/mo; Pro $249/mo crossed out, $124/mo; Enterprise $499/mo crossed out, $249/mo, so 50% off the list price in the app. The text says: Try any plan free for 30 days. You pay $0 today. Your first charge would be on December 17, 2026, and you can cancel anytime before then from your Shopify admin. The discount is temporary and tied to the store; the App Store listing shows $99, $249 and $499 without a discount. Sorted collections per plan: Demo 2, Basic 25, Pro 100, Enterprise 1000; processing schedule Demo 60 min, Basic 30, Pro 20, Enterprise 10. Demo has no Customers Also Bought recipes and no device analytics. The App Store listing now shows the collection counts in the right column; the dossier still describes the mislabelled plan cards seen in October. Checkout: the free Demo plan was chosen, the paid plans were not clicked, so no Shopify approval screen, no total, no test charge and no card field was seen. Nothing was approved. Cancelling: no paid plan was started. In Settings, Apps, Uninstall opened the dialog Uninstall Dynasort?, which says that the app can no longer be used, that data managed by the app will be deleted and that a request will be sent to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information. A reason for uninstalling is required (Testing multiple apps was chosen). The app was uninstalled at about 22:22 after the evidence was complete and is gone from the installed apps. Not tested: the paid plans and the free trial, the A/B test, a sold out product moving to the bottom, variant sorting, recommendations, the effect in the online store (only the Shopify admin was checked), a large catalogue, Insights (data appears after 24 hours) and Sort rotation. Clean up: the collection order was set back to Most relevant, the Dynasort Status was set to Off, Processing had been switched On in the app and disappeared with the uninstall, the app was uninstalled and our own tab was closed. No other app was touched. The price fields are not changed here. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app did not sort until Processing was switched On in Settings, which the app only said after the status was set to Active. The first synchronisation took more than 7 minutes (the app said about 5). The sort choice of the collection in Shopify changes to Manually, and after the app was switched off Shopify stayed on Manually until the sort choice was reset by hand. The paid plans showed a temporary discount in the app that the App Store listing does not show, and the dossier still describes the mislabelled plan cards of October.
